run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:25:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real, continuously produced errors: frontend-proxy's own ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR at a steady ~1/min (ERROR counter 557 at 00:58:00 -> 588 at 01:33:00; 20m increases of 15.6-22.6), and the proxy's access log shows the matching failures as HTTP 503 with response flag `UC` (`upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`) on many different routes (/, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products/..., /api/recommendations), with the upstream named `frontend`. The number of 503 log lines observed (21 in 00:58:59-01:13:23 plus 10 in 01:17:13-01:29:27 = 31) matches the 31 increment of the ERROR counter. The errors are therefore frontend-proxy->frontend connection terminations, not backend failures visible in traces: no error spans exist for frontend or any other backend in 01:15:45-01:31:45 apart from flagd EventStream spans on ad/fraud-detection/recommendation, and p99 span durations stayed in the hundreds of ms. All otel-demo deployments are 1/1 ready, pods are Running with restartCount 0 on frontend and frontend-proxy, memory and CPU are well below limits, and all flagd fault-injection flags are `off`, so an enabled fault flag, crash/OOM or resource exhaustion is not supported. The errors existed ~27 minutes before the alert start (00:58:59 vs 01:25:45) and continued after it, so the alert appears to fire on a chronic non-zero error rate rather than on a new outage; the exact alert expression, and therefore how the reported 0.0333 is computed, could not be verified because Prometheus exposes no rules and the frontend's own logs are unreadable. Root cause is left null: the terminating peer is the frontend, but the specific reason it closes those connections (candidate: Envoy/Node keep-alive idle-timeout race) is a hypothesis, not established.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans report STATUS_CODE_ERROR continuously at about 1 per minute: 20-minute increases ranged 22.56 (01:16:45) to 15.58 (01:31:45), against 20-minute UNSET counts of ~11,745-13,858, and the raw ERROR counter rose 557 at 00:58:00 to 588 at 01:33:00 (31 increments).

frontend-proxy's own access log records the errors as `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` with the upstream field reading `frontend`, on multiple routes: 21 such lines between 00:58:59.988 and 01:13:23.124 (e.g. GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO, GET /api/cart, GET /api/recommendations?productIds=L9ECAV7KIM, GET /api/data/?contextKeys=assembly, GET /), and 10 more between 01:17:13.550 and 01:29:27.955 (GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z, /api/cart, /api/recommendations?productIds=0PUK6V6EV0, /, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel, /api/products/66VCHSJNUP).

The 503 log-line count matches the span-metric error count: 21 lines in 00:58:59-01:13:23 plus 10 lines in 01:17:13-01:29:27 equals 31, the same as the 557->588 increment of the frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter over 00:58:00-01:33:00.

In 01:15:45-01:31:45 the only services with STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increases were ad, fraud-detection and recommendation on their flagd `EventStream` spans (1.0-2.1 per 20 minutes) plus frontend-proxy ingress (18.46-22.56 per 20 minutes); no error spans were reported for frontend or any other backend service.

frontend-proxy and frontend latency show no degradation: p99 span duration stayed roughly 1.15-1.68 s for frontend-proxy ingress, 0.3-1.5 s for frontend routes such as GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout, and 0.03-0.13 s for product-catalog GetProduct/ListProducts across 01:00-01:32.
All 21 otel-demo deployments report readyReplicas=availableReplicas=updatedReplicas=1, including frontend and frontend-proxy.

All otel-demo pods are Running; frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt have restartCount 0 and started at 2026-11-18T00:45 (05x), and both pods show Ready/ContainersReady/PodScheduled conditions True with empty lastState; only fraud-detection shows 1 restart.

The only events in the authorized window belong to cluster objects in namespace data-recorders (Jobs Completed/SuccessfulCreate, PVC provisioning, one Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, one ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, one Pod Killing); no event names an otel-demo object.

In ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config every fault-injection flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

frontend and frontend-proxy are not resource-exhausted: frontend working set was 121.0-123.0 MiB against a 200Mi limit and frontend-proxy 19.4-20.1 MiB against 50Mi; CPU use was ~0.048-0.053 cores for frontend (limit 100m) and ~0.0135-0.0143 cores for frontend-proxy (limit 30m).

frontend container CPU was throttled for 26-36% of CFS periods throughout 00:58-01:32 (e.g. 0.353 at 00:58:00 and 0.275 at 01:32:00), while frontend-proxy throttling was 4.9-7.3% over the same period, i.e. both were steady before and during the alert.

Three 503 UC lines occurred within 250 ms at 01:25:21.864, 01:25:21.965 and 01:25:22.114 (GET /api/recommendations, GET /, GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4), about 24 seconds before the alert's 01:25:45 start; earlier bursts were two lines at 01:23:58.542/.689 and three lines at 01:07:00.367/.674/01:07:01.340.

The only NetworkPolicy in the cluster, otel-demo/frontend-block-all-ports, selects the frontend pods with policyTypes [Ingress] and contains a single empty ingress rule (`ingress: [{}]`), which matches all sources and ports; it is not evidence of traffic being blocked, and ~99.9% of proxied requests succeed.

No backend outage explains the errors: frontend produced no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, its latency was stable, its pod was Ready with 0 restarts, and the failures are connection terminations on many unrelated routes rather than failures of one downstream service.

The 503 UC errors are most likely an upstream keep-alive race: Envoy (frontend-proxy) reuses an idle HTTP/1 connection to the frontend at the moment the frontend's server closes it, so requests fail before any response starts. This fits the sub-second failure durations (8-849 ms), the random mix of routes, the repeated tiny bursts and the fact that errors began with the load (~00:58:59) and stayed at ~0.8-1.5/min. The actual idle/keep-alive settings are baked into the container images and were not readable, so this is not verified.

The alert's 0.0333 value may correspond to a short-window ratio: the 3 errors within 250 ms at 01:25:21-01:25:22 occurred 24 s before the 01:25:45 alert start. The evaluation window and denominator used by the alerting pipeline could not be read, so this link is unproven.

Fault injection via flagd was considered and rejected as the cause: every flag in otel-demo/flagd-config is at defaultVariant "off", including cartFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure which would map to the failing routes.

A crash, OOM or rollout of frontend or frontend-proxy was considered and rejected: both pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState, started 00:45 and never replaced during the window, and no otel-demo events (Killing, Unhealthy, Evicted, OOMKilling, SuccessfulCreate/Delete) were recorded.
Resource exhaustion of frontend-proxy was considered and rejected: it uses ~19.4-20.1 MiB of its 50Mi memory limit and ~0.0135-0.0143 of its 0.03-core CPU limit, with only 4.9-7.3% CFS throttling.

gaps: The alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate (37ebc98e-4431-41aa-afdd-4dbaf259ca1f-t0:b9ad01b1-85bc-42c9-b3ce-cb567c52752e) and for an unfiltered query (ce325e74-2673-4357-b349-d15c630d5258-t1:53d7079b-3a64-4524-bcbe-7dfb1eace6d3), so the alert expression, evaluation window and how the 0.0333 value is derived (and why it started at 01:25:45 while errors existed since 00:58:59) are unknown.

The frontend pod's application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh in 01:10-01:33 and 01:28-01:29:40 returned no_data with 0 lines read (cb96e236-6305-4baf-9253-ed5d6bc13819-t1:ebf78337-4de6-4e88-8cb6-3a103ebfe46d, 4c9138de-423a-4cf5-bffb-1853bf9cc1a6-t0:22c3db06-5ff6-4975-8e16-7b5e1b8e5f0e), so the reason the frontend closes upstream connections is not observable from its own logging.

Short-window rate queries on the frontend-proxy ERROR counter were inconsistent with the raw counter: sum(increase(...[1m])) returned 0 at every minute from 00:59 to 01:31 while the raw counter rose 557->588, so per-minute error rates from this metric cannot be trusted.

The Envoy upstream idle timeout and the frontend server's keep-alive/headers timeout settings are baked into the container images and were not readable, so the keep-alive-race hypothesis cannot be confirmed or refuted.
No change history is available for this environment (change_history is not integrated), so whether anything changed at the alert onset 01:25:45 could not be checked.

Trace evidence is a biased, incomplete sample: the 640-span frontend-proxy search was too large to read whole (c086e0f0-b3cb-43ed-9ddc-c92186714816-t0:fd42da45-152e-4450-836b-1938f5a353fd, truncated) and tag searches for error=true (ce325e74-2673-4357-b349-d15c630d5258-t0:dbaba00a-e593-404f-89e5-8d669a6ef696), http.status_code=500 (cf984243-2c0b-4a81-bad0-bcfea9d26432-t1:63b4d730-96ff-4c42-bb93-4dcfac73f406), http.status_code=404 (48e67134-4430-4275-8c43-221a0414e63d-t0:2288e118-4448-4cd0-a4d1-a61a486e09c4) and otel.status_code=ERROR (f8867984-dbfd-4452-9574-3b414ffa39dc-t1:0315f749-8234-4b55-b3d7-1a90360ecb70) returned no_data, so no complete call chain for a failed 503 request was obtained; those requests left no upstream response and are represented only by Envoy access-log lines.

The proxy's truncated log stream (f8867984-dbfd-4452-9574-3b414ffa39dc-t0:21b5324c-eb41-4422-bb65-cac690d8ef57, limit: newest 60 of 1229 matching lines) and the 4 MiB read cut at 01:16:47.265144Z mean log lines after those cuts are unknown, not absent.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule (or the alerting pipeline's expression) to confirm the numerator, denominator and evaluation window behind the 0.0333 value and to see whether a threshold above a small non-zero floor is warranted.

Compare frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream idle timeout / max requests per connection with the frontend server's keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout, and align them (or shorten Envoy's upstream idle timeout) to remove the connection-reuse race.

Enable or capture frontend access/error logging around a failing request (using request IDs from the Envoy log lines, e.g. 39e1c25c-73e6-970d-bf7f-6d71819ead7e) to confirm whether the frontend intentionally closes the connection.

If the 503 rate is accepted as background noise for this demo workload, treat the alert as tuning work rather than an incident; otherwise raise the alert threshold above the observed ~0.1-0.2% error ratio.
